name: Dora Villa
life: “I still remember taking the bill from my father when I finally earned more than him.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Studio Boulevard, where Dora waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I used to be the kid with no money at this party. I overpaid the bill before anyone could stop me.
appearance: Back on the street, look for a cropped bottle-green coat and a replacement button a shade darker than the others. Dora has one cheek that creases before the other, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Dora folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing during a conversation.
personality: Dora can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To take the pressure off the host without embarrassing them.
family: Cyrus Keller is Dora’s younger cousin. Dora puts the kettle on. Cyrus chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The third bedroom*, Cyrus says, “I have shared a room with my brother ever since the night we left.”
connections: Gerard Ito. One relative wants to admit what supper costs. The other has already covered more than a fair share.

reactions.situation: A waiter offers to split one birthday dessert among everybody
reactions.response: Dora checks that the birthday guest likes the dessert before calculating the portions.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Dora stays with the rider after the people who saw the fall start drifting away.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Dora asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
